item.title: A 30-year-old fossil was hiding bones from a mysterious ancient sea monster
item.description: Fossils collected in Osaka more than 30 years ago have revealed a surprise hiding in plain sight: four previously unrecognized bones from a giant Cretaceous mosasaur. Among them is the first confirmed premaxilla—the frontmost bone of the upper jaw—ever identified in a Japanese mosasaur fossil. Even more intriguing, parts of the skull show unusual anatomical features that don’t match known mosasaurs, raising the possibility that the remains belong to an entirely new species. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.description: Introduced to Newfoundland more than a century ago as a food source, moose have surged in numbers, drastically altering the island’s forest ecosystem. The absence of natural predators allows these massive herbivores to devour young trees at alarming rates. To mitigate this issue and safeguard habitats, hunting quotas are thoughtfully managed, seeking to achieve a harmony between ecological integrity and human needs. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: The ground beneath Poland's wind turbines became nesting grounds for wild bees
item.description: In Poland, the bases of wind turbines have emerged as surprising havens for pollinators. Research highlights that these zones foster a thriving community of wild bees and a variety of plant species. The bare gravel and low maintenance create perfect nesting sites for ground-nesting bees. While butterflies opt for grasslands, both flies and grasslands flourish equally in these overlooked yet vital habitats for biodiversity on farmland. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: In 1958, 58 pigs were removed from Clipperton, helping seabirds grow to 137,000
item.description: Feral pigs introduced to Clipperton Island devastated seabird populations and land crabs. Ornithologist Kenneth Stager removed fifty-eight pigs, allowing the ecosystem to gradually recover. This removal helped the seabird colony grow from 650 to over 137,000 birds. Later, black rats arrived, impacting the island's vegetation and bird populations negatively. Clipperton's story highlights invasive species' profound ecological effects on islands. Fuente: The Times of India - World.
